MC	<p>1491_b4cc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580f;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #77580f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #056591;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580f;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #77580f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c55a_e2dc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cx, ++, cx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #305ea1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cm, ++, cm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f442_bbc4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580f;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #77580f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bt, ++, bt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>dee3_d271</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b7a8_09ba</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933768;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933768;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933768;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, de, ++, de"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">9,200</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>5d39_aeff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #056591;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933768;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #933768;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893590;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9566_e090</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dt, ++, dt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983e1a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0c7132;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6fbe_ba0b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0c7132;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #305ea1;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c02;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #305ea1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b071_7bdf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0c7132;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933768;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933768;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933768;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, by, ++, by"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>399d_abaf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kn, ++, kn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3461_e8b1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7042a8;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7042a8;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7042a8;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bm, ++, bm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580f;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #77580f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7042a8;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7042a8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d823_dbe2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #056591;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, wy, ++, wy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6156_b177</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983e1a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ca5d_d3a0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580f;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #77580f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #305ea1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, rt, ++, rt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>988b_7998</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893590;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, af, ++, af"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933768;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #933768;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>448c_7d0b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893590;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mp, ++, mp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c76f_45f9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8a4c02;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kn, ++, kn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>813d_42c4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4c02;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>60ce_7f1e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f313e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f313e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f490_3a9d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0c7132;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0c7132;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bb5f_9195</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hm, ++, hm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b9f1_f03e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8a4c02;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cy, ++, cy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6758_c4d0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>2e4a_4194</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #305ea1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ry, ++, ry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>13d4_ec6a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4c02;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c02;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056591;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #056591;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>cc8d_e252</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893590;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ae, ++, ae"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>be64_6e8a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #983e1a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>0bfc_75a3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983e1a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e1a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4d4ebb;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4ebb;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bm, ++, bm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2628_034d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893590;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893590;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype.
